summary: CSV importer (5-platform parser refactor) tested end-to-end against the public preview. Backend: 15/15 parser unit tests in /app/backend/tests/test_csv_importer.py PASS, and 13/14 new live integration tests in /app/backend/tests/test_import_integration.py PASS against the deployed API. Regression: 122/122 (Stage 6B+6C+6D + csv_importer unit suite) PASS. Frontend (Playwright on the public preview URL): admin login → /import flow validated for all three branches — Tokeet (booking import, banner + TOK- reservation id + 'Confirm import (1 new rows)' label), Guestpoint Person Detail (enrichment banner with exact spec text + 'Confirm enrichment (1 guests)' label + preview-enrichment-body), Preno (booking import, PRE-...-SMITH reservation id, raw_source 'Booking.com' from @guest.booking.com domain rule, value rendered as '—', cancelled 'No'). ONE backend parser bug found and reported: Guestpoint Person Detail / Customer Export date columns (First Stay, Last Stay, Date of Birth) are parsed without dayfirst=True, so DD/MM/YYYY values like '01/05/2026' (1 May 2026) come back as '2026-01-05' (5 Jan 2026). All other parser behaviour, tolerance rules, encoding fallback, RBAC and enrichment-vs-booking branching match spec.

minor.endpoint: POST /api/import/preview (Guestpoint Person Detail + Guestpoint Customer Export)
minor.issue: parse_guestpoint_person_detail / parse_guestpoint_customer_export call parse_date(raw.get('First Stay')) / parse_date(raw.get('Last Stay')) / parse_date(raw.get('Date of Birth')) at /app/backend/csv_importer.py lines 332-333 and 360 WITHOUT dayfirst=True. Spec ('Guestpoint Person Detail dates also DD/MM/YYYY') says these are DD/MM/YYYY but pandas falls back to MM/DD interpretation for ambiguous values. Repro: '01/05/2026' (= 1 May 2026 DD/MM) is parsed to '2026-01-05' (= 5 Jan 2026). Existing pytest test_guestpoint_person_detail_flow doesn't assert specific dates so this is latent. Fix: pass dayfirst=True (and optionally fmts=['%d/%m/%Y']) for those three calls.

Tolerance rule keep_row correctly skips ONLY when guest_name AND checkin_date are both empty — validated with both an empty-TOTAL row (kept, value=null) and a fully blank row (skipped, row_errors populated).
Encoding fallback works: 0xe0 Latin-1 byte for 'Andrà' silently decodes without 400; garbage bytes also decode via latin-1 replace and return 200.

DD/MM/YYYY handling is inconsistent: Tokeet/VikBooking/Preno parsers all pass dayfirst=True OR explicit fmts to parse_date, but the two Guestpoint enrichment parsers (lines 332-333, 360) call parse_date(value) with no dayfirst hint — defaults to dayfirst=False. Single-character fix.

rca of the issue: GP Person Detail DD/MM/YYYY misparse — root cause: /app/backend/csv_importer.py parse_guestpoint_person_detail (lines 332-333) calls parse_date(raw.get('First Stay')) and parse_date(raw.get('Last Stay')) with positional-only args. parse_date defaults dayfirst=False, so the fallback `pd.to_datetime(s, errors='coerce', dayfirst=False)` (line 128) interprets '01/05/2026' as MM/DD → '2026-01-05'. Same defect on line 360 for the Customer Export Date of Birth. The other platform parsers (Tokeet line 222-224 use explicit %d %b fmts, VikBooking line 247-249 pass dayfirst=True + %d/%m/%Y, Preno line 281-282 pass dayfirst=True + %d/%m/%Y) all correctly honour the Australian DD/MM/YYYY convention. Reproduction: POST /api/import/preview with the gp_person.csv fixture in /tmp/csv_samples/ → rows[0].last_stay == '2026-01-05' (wrong) for input '01/05/2026'. Mitigation: change lines 332-333 to `parse_date(raw.get('First Stay'), ['%d/%m/%Y'], dayfirst=True)` (same for Last Stay), and line 360 to `parse_date(raw.get('Date of Birth'), ['%d/%m/%Y'], dayfirst=True)`. This also silences the existing 'Parsing dates in %d/%m/%Y format when dayfirst=False' UserWarning logged during pytest.
